text: §10§ A binary tree is a hierarchical data structure in which each node has at most two children, usually called left and right, with a single root node at the top. It's the foundation for structures like binary search trees and heaps, where operations typically cost O(h) for tree height h — and O(log n) when the tree stays balanced.
